scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: The Connection Lab’s fictional account uses a password and a separate approved sign-in confirmation. Neel proposes adding another password instead. Tara asks whether two remembered secrets provide the same separation as a different kind of safeguard controlled through an approved device.
scenes.speech: The Connection Lab’s fictional account uses a password and a separate approved sign-in confirmation. Neel proposes adding another password instead. scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: A password is something known; a registered device can provide a different factor. No safeguard makes an account impossible to misuse, and an unexpected approval should not be accepted just to clear a notification. Students use a teacher-supervised simulation rather than real accounts.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: Recovery information helps regain access but can also expose it. The teacher keeps a fictional recovery envelope through the school’s approved process, separate from shared worksheets. The class practises getting help after an unfamiliar request without displaying or forwarding any secret value.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: No sign-in was started, and a trusted adult is available. Approving the notification would authorise an unexplained request. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: No sign-in was started, and a trusted adult is available. Approving the notification would authorise an unexplained request. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.dialogue: A confirmation appears when Neel is not signing in. What next?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Decline the unexpected request and tell the trusted adult, then review access through known account settings. A second safeguard works only when approvals are handled carefully.
scenes.speech: Decline the unexpected request and tell the trusted adult, then review access through known account settings. A second safeguard works only when approvals are handled carefully.
scenes.dialogue: Keep recovery secrets separate from shared classroom materials.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate different sign-in safeguards, then private recovery information, then unexpected approval requests. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
